core_obligations: Let e be the ramification index of C over B; if e = 1 the first alternative holds, and otherwise conclude e = p using the inequality and ramification-index lemmas, which also shows that the residue fields of B and C agree (proof lines 34698-34701).
Choose a uniformizer pi_C of C and write pi_C^p = u pi for a unit u of C; since pi_C^p lies in L, conclude u lies in B^*, and record that M = L[pi_C] (proof lines 34702-34704).
Suppose there is an integer m >= 0 with u equal to the displayed sum of terms b_i^p pi^i for i < m plus b pi^m, where b has image in kappa_B which is not a p-th power (proof lines 34707-34711).

Choose an extension K_1/K from the degree-q construction with n = m + 2, let pi' be the uniformizer of the integral closure A_1 satisfying pi = (pi')^p + (pi')^{np} a, let B_1 be the integral closure of B in L tensor_K K_1, and note that A_1 -> B_1 is weakly unramified (proof lines 34712-34719).
Verify the displayed identity in B_1 expressing u pi as a p-th power plus b (pi')^{(m+1)p} plus (pi')^{np} b_1, a computation the author states is omitted (proof lines 34720-34726).

Conclude that M_1 is obtained from L_1 by adjoining a p-th root of b + (pi')^{n-m-1} b_1, and since the residue field of B_1 equals that of B, use the pre-purely-inseparable-case lemma to get that M_1/L_1 has degree p and C_1 is weakly unramified over B_1, giving the third alternative (proof lines 34727-34736).

If no such integer m exists, conclude that u is a p-th power in the pi-adic completion of B_1, and since B is Nagata that u is a p-th power in B_1, so the second alternative C = B[pi^{1/p}] holds (proof lines 34739-34743).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a tower A in B in C of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields K in L in M, a uniformizer pi of A, and assumes B is Nagata, A in B is weakly unramified, and M is a degree p purely inseparable extension of L; it concludes that one of three alternatives holds: that A -> C is weakly unramified; that C = B[pi^{1/p}]; or that there exists a degree p separable extension K_1/K totally ramified with respect to A such that L_1 = L tensor_K K_1 and M_1 = M tensor_K K_1 are fields and the maps of integral closures A_1 -> B_1 -> C_1 are weakly unramified extensions of discrete valuation rings (source lines 34675-34695). The proof is a case analysis controlled by a p-adic expansion. Letting e be the ramification index of C over B, the proof disposes of e = 1 immediately, and otherwise observes that e = p by the inequality and ramification-index lemmas, which implies that the residue fields of B and C agree; choosing a uniformizer pi_C of C one writes pi_C^p = u pi for a unit u of C, and since pi_C^p lies in L one gets u in B^*, as well as M = L[pi_C] (proof lines 34698-34704). The first substantial case is when there is an integer m >= 0 with u expanded as the displayed sum of p-th powers of elements of B times powers of pi plus a term b pi^m whose coefficient b has image in kappa_B which is not a p-th power; the proof then chooses an extension K_1/K from the degree-q construction with n = m + 2, denotes pi' the corresponding uniformizer with pi = (pi')^p + (pi')^{np} a, notes that A_1 -> B_1 is weakly unramified, and computes in B_1 the displayed identity expressing u pi as a p-th power plus b (pi')^{(m+1)p} plus (pi')^{np} b_1, a computation the author states is omitted (proof lines 34707-34726). From that identity the proof concludes that M_1 is obtained from L_1 by adjoining a p-th root of b + (pi')^{n-m-1} b_1, and since the residue field of B_1 equals that of B, the pre-purely-inseparable-case lemma gives that M_1/L_1 has degree p and C_1 is weakly unramified over B_1, which is the third alternative (proof lines 34727-34736). The second case is the complement: if no such m exists, then u is a p-th power in the pi-adic completion of B_1, and since B is Nagata this makes u a p-th power in B_1 itself, so the second alternative C = B[pi^{1/p}] holds (proof lines 34739-34743). The non-routine content is the p-adic expansion dichotomy and the explicitly computed identity in B_1.
